;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[July 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***At least six civilians are killed when their vehicle hits a [[roadside bomb]] in [[Ghazni Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. A [[provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] [[government of Afghanistan|government]] spokesman blames the [[Taliban]] though no group claimed responsibility. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/07/11/Roadside-bomb-kills-6-Afghan-civilians-in-east-says-Ghazni-province-official.html (AP via Al Arabiya)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**The [[United Nations Security Council]] approves [[humanitarian aid|aid]] deliveries to northwest [[Syria]] through one [[Syria-Turkey border|border]] crossing with [[Turkey]], a day after its authorization for the six-year-long humanitarian operation ended. [[Russia]] and [[China]] abstain today on this week's fifth attempt to approve this help. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-un/on-fifth-attempt-u-n-security-council-renews-syria-aid-via-turkey-idUSKCN24C0U8 (Reuters)]
*[[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] commemorates 25 years since the [[Srebrenica massacre]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53374935 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
***[[Disney's Animal Kingdom|Animal Kingdom]] and [[Magic Kingdom]] reopens at [[Walt Disney World]] with new safety guidelines despite rising cases in [[Florida]]. Masks are expected to be mandatory and capacity is expected to be limited. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/07/11/walt-disney-world-orlando-reopening-during-covid-19-how-to-stay-safe.html (CNBC)] [https://www.wsj.com/articles/disney-world-reopens-with-masks-and-without-lines-11594472403 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*A sealed copy of the 1985 [[Nintendo Entertainment System]] game ''[[Super Mario Bros.]]'' sells for [[United States dollar|US$]]114,000, a world record for a video game. [https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2020/07/this_sealed_copy_of_super_mario_bros_just_sold_for_usd114000?fbclid=IwAR261kSSkVtMgdkqP9tnvICaurEr4XMKdJTh4Xr4tYjPn7uKXTzSNh8bDHM (Nintendo Life)]
*The [[World Council of Churches]], which counts 350 churches as members, calls on [[President of Turkey|Turkey's President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] to reverse his decision to turn the celebrated [[Hagia Sophia]] museum back into a mosque. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53375739 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*In the second case in a week in [[Australia]], a surfing teenage boy is killed by a [[shark]] near [[Grafton, New South Wales]]. [https://apnews.com/ffdbe5b9ffead4611a2a0eef966f5282 (AP News)]
*A fire breaks out at the [[Mission San Gabriel Arcángel]] in [[San Gabriel, California]], US, resulting in the collapse of its roof and considerable damage to the nearly 250-year-old building's interior. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/11/us/california-san-gabriel-mission-fire.amp.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Louisiana]]
****[[Governor of Louisiana|Louisiana Governor]] [[John Bel Edwards]] issues an executive order requiring people to wear [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|face masks]] in public. [https://www.axios.com/louisiana-face-mask-mandate-86704f4f-2a52-452d-9144-e4ec52d6df23.html (Axios)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
****The COVID-19 hospitalizations and average three-day death toll in [[New York (state)|New York]] reach lower levels for the first time since March. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-york-coronavirus-cases-death-toll-lowest-3-day-average-since-march-16/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Karnataka]]
****The [[Government of Karnataka|Karnataka government]] announces that [[Bangalore|Bengaluru]] will be on [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in India|lockdown]] from July 14 to July 22. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/bengaluru-to-be-under-complete-lockdown-from-july-14-to-22-1.1594495057372 (Gulf News)]
***Indian film actor [[Amitabh Bachchan]] is hospitalized after testing positive for [[COVID-19]]. His son, [[Abhishek Bachchan]], also tests positive. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/11/entertainment/amitabh-bachchan-bollywood-superstar-coronavirus-trnd/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[South African Police Service|Police]] respond to a shooting and [[hostage]] situation at a [[International Pentecostal Holiness Church (Africa)|pentecostal]] [[church (building)|church]] in [[Zuurbekom]], [[Gauteng]], [[South Africa]]. At least five people are killed. South African police free an undetermined number of hostages, and arrest more than 40 people. Among those arrested were members of the police, defense forces and correctional services. The attackers reportedly were part of a splinter group in a leadership dispute at the long-troubled church. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-safrica-violence/five-killed-as-hostages-taken-at-south-african-church-idUSKCN24C0FB?il=0 (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53375607 (BBC News)] [https://apnews.com/086dd45f4eaff2d4b4878ccd7d73d7ed (AP)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Protests against responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[2020–2022 Serbian protests|Serbia COVID-19 protests and riots]]
***[[Serbians]] protest for a fourth consecutive day; the protest initially started out against the government [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] measures but would morph into anti-government protests. 71 people are arrested. [https://www.dw.com/en/serbia-protesters-try-to-storm-parliament-amid-fresh-unrest/a-54135350 (DW News)]
*[[2020 Hong Kong pro-democracy primaries]]
**Election starts for [[pro-democracy]] politicians and activists to choose representatives to run in the upcoming [[2020 Hong Kong legislative election|legislative election]] in September. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-election/hong-kong-opposition-kicks-off-primary-elections-under-shadow-of-security-law-idUSKCN24C04Z?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] Justice Minister Celestin Tunda resigns following disputes with [[President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|President]] [[Félix Tshisekedi]] over Tunda and allies's proposal to allow politicians more control over criminal prosecution cases. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/dr-congo-justice-minister-celestin-tunda-resigns-dispute-200711151050599.html (Al Jazeera)]
*Thousands of protesters march in [[Khabarovsk]], [[Khabarovsk Krai]], [[Russia]], against Thursday's arrest of [[Liberal Democratic Party of Russia|LDPR]] [[Governor of Khabarovsk Krai|governor]] [[Sergey Furgal]] for allegedly organizing the murder of [[entrepreneur]]s 15 years ago. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-politics-governor/russian-city-marches-in-support-of-detained-regional-governor-idUSKCN24C0D1?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Mali]] [[list of heads of state of Mali|President]] [[Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta]] announces dissolution of the [[Politics_of_Mali#Judicial_branch|constitutional court]] in an attempt to calm unrest that saw four people killed in anti-government protests in the capital [[Bamako]] on Friday. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-07-12/mali-president-dissolves-constitutional-court-after-unrest (Bloomberg)]  [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53378433 (BBC News)]
